newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-TEENAGE SENSATION KOURNIKOVA DOWNS FRENCH OPEN CHAMPION.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-TEENAGE SENSATION KOURNIKOVA DOWNS FRENCH OPEN CHAMPION.

text.p: Wimbledon's new teenage sensation Anna Kournikova trampled French Open champion Iva Majoli at Wimbledon on Wednesday with a display of ice-cool, athletic tennis.
The eye-catching Russian, who celebrated her 16th birthday only three weeks ago, showed no signs of awe and wonder on the centre court as she powered her way to a 7-6 6-4 victory.
Kournikova was joined in the semifinals by Jana Novotna, veteran of 12 Wimbledons who dispatched Indonesia's Yayuk Basuki with no less strength of purpose 6-3 6-3.
With deadly accuracy and spectacular speed across the court, the unseeded Kournikova, ranked 42 in the world, punished Majoli's serve and pounced on every stray ball.
The 19-year-old Croatian fourth seed, who had never won a match on grass before this year's Wimbledon but had improved her technique with every game here, found herself pinned to the baseline.
She lost the tie-break 7-1, then dropped two service games in the second set.
Kournikova, who trains in Florida at the Nick Bolletieri school which also moulded Andre Agassi and Monica Seles, produced two blistering forehand returns to take the match.
Only Jennifer Capriati has reached a Wimbledon semifinal at a younger age than the Russian. She was some nine months younger in 1991.
The 28-year-old Novotna, whose own athleticism and finely honed serve-and-volley style suit the grass well, showed no sign of her notorious nerves on Wednesday.
Her serve was on song -- she put in some 75 percent of her first serves compared with less than 50 per cent for Basuki -- and her volleys were crisp and inch-perfect.
"I thought that I was playing very decent solid tennis and had the match under control from the start," Novotna, seeded three, said.
Basuki, ranked 26 in the world and playing her first Grand Slam quarter-final, had no answer.

The Czech, who has reached the quarter-finals here five times and the semifinals once, is best remembered here for the 1993 final against Steffi Graf when she wept on the Duchess of Kent's shoulder after throwing away a 4-1 lead in the deciding set.

But on Wednesday she was relaxed. "I was feeling very confident coming into the tournament," she said. I'll go out there in the semifinals and enjoy myself and entertain the crowd. That's what it's all about."
